note: Traditions whose job was to make you want something. This deck is stocked on a different property from the read deck, and the difference is measured rather than assumed: an analysis of all 102 three-star worlds found them overwhelmingly beloved, reproduced graphics with a time of day, a place you can stand in, and a subculture that loved them. A dial-up bulletin board at 2 a.m., a printing darkroom under amber safelight, a rail concourse split-flap board at rush hour. That property predicts a flagship here and anti-predicted in the read wave, which is the clearest evidence the two modes want different things.

bar:
## The persuade bar, which is not the bar for other modes

This world will be dealt to landing pages, pricing, and campaigns. It has one
requirement the other modes do not, and it is the single most reliable failure
the catalog has measured.

**It must be able to make one thing dominate.** Every one of six worlds in an
earlier wave failed here, and they failed in the same words: "nothing can
emphasize the plan you want sold", "all persuasion runs at 12px", "no hero is
possible", "rank collapsed". Documentation hierarchy is sequence and heading;
persuasion needs one element to outrank everything near it, and the aesthetic
prohibitions routinely remove the usual tools by forbidding colour-as-state,
capping type sizes, or banning scale.

So name the emphasis mechanism explicitly, in the rules, and check it survives
your own prohibitions. One world made rank the size of a cleared cavity and the
cavity was invisible in two of its three materials, which turned it into a page
design. Check yours in every material your palette rule allows, at a wall size
and on a phone, and in greyscale.

**And it must be able to carry prose.** Persuasion is sentences, and a
drenched or textured ground has no obligation to carry them unless you say how.
Four transfers measured this failing: body text at 77% ink coverage, a control
label at 1.13:1 against its own state colour, two adjacent prices at 1.31:1.

**What earns a flagship here.** The catalog's three-star worlds are
overwhelmingly beloved things: they carry a time of day, a place you can stand
in, and a subculture that loved them. Your assigned tradition has that in it
already. Put it in the spark and let it drive the material, rather than
describing a graphic style with the affection removed.
